instructions:
Pharaoh answers structural questions about mapped repos from a graph of each repo's default branch: functions, callers, modules, dependencies, endpoints, cron jobs and reachability, for TypeScript, JavaScript and Python. No source code is stored.

## Which tool answers which question

Pharaoh answers these questions from the graph:

| Question | Tool |
|---|---|
| Does X already exist? Where is Y implemented? | search_functions |
| What calls X? What breaks if I change it? Which endpoints or cron jobs reach it? | get_blast_radius |
| What's in this module, what does it depend on, who calls into it? | get_module_context |
| Is this code dead or wired in? What can I delete? | get_unused_code |
| How is the repo laid out? Which module owns this? What's the repo called? | get_codebase_map |
| Several of these at once (planning a change, reviewing a PR) | pharaoh_recon |

The graph reflects the default branch at its last mapped push, and a response says when a newer push is still being mapped. Grep and file reads cover what it leaves out: code that isn't on the default branch yet (other branches, uncommitted edits), literal text (strings, error messages, config values, comments, non-code files) and renames, which change every reference, tests and mocks included.

## Repos

Repos are mapped through the Pharaoh GitHub App, installed on the account or org that owns them: `https://github.com/apps/pharaoh-so/installations/new`. The App reads the repositories it is installed on and the organization's membership; its only write permission is posting check results. Live repos re-map on every push. search_functions accepts any of the user's mapped repo names.

Tools take the short repo name in their `repo` parameter (e.g. "pharaoh", not "org/pharaoh"). Unambiguous short names resolve automatically. A name that doesn't resolve returns suggestions and the user's repos grouped by organization.

## Account

pharaoh_account shows the plan and which repos are live. pharaoh_manage_repo switches a free workspace's live repo, or queues a re-map of a live repo.

tools.name: get_codebase_map
tools.title: Codebase Map
tools.description:
A repo's architecture in one call.

CALL THIS WHEN:
• Getting a repo's overall structure, or which module owns something
• The repo's exact name in Pharaoh isn't known

RETURNS: Modules with file counts and LOC, module dependencies with two-way ones flagged, the 5 files changed most in 90 days, endpoints with handler files (first 50), convention entry points (first 30), and risk signals (high-risk functions without direct test links, exact clones, cycles).

repo.description: Repository name — one of your connected repos.

include_metrics.description: List the 10 most-changed files instead of 5

tools.name: pharaoh_recon
tools.title: Codebase Recon
tools.description:
Several Pharaoh queries in one call, run in parallel: codebase map, module profiles, function searches, blast radius and module dependency paths.

CALL THIS WHEN:
• Planning a change, reviewing a PR or assessing architecture, when the modules and functions to check are known

RETURNS: Each requested section in one response, as the single-purpose tools return it. Per call: up to 5 modules, 3 searches, 3 blast radius targets, 3 dependency pairs.

repo.description: Repository name — one of your connected repos.

dependencies.description: Module pairs to trace a dependency path between

tools.name: get_module_context
tools.title: Module Context
tools.description:
One module's profile: what it contains, depends on and is called by.

CALL THIS WHEN:
• Changing code in a module, or planning a change to it
• Finding what a module exports, depends on, or which code calls into it

RETURNS: Files, LOC, exported signatures with complexity, imports in and out, DB tables, endpoints, cron jobs, env vars, and callers in other modules, grouped by module.

repo.description: Repository name — one of your connected repos.

tools.name: get_blast_radius
tools.title: Blast Radius
tools.description:
What a change to a function, file or module reaches.

CALL THIS WHEN:
• Changing a signature, refactoring or deleting code
• Finding the callers or detected endpoints a change reaches

RETURNS: Risk, production callers by module/file, endpoints, cron jobs and DB operations, through direct and indirect calls. Hops are the shortest detected path within the requested depth (1–5). Test-file callers are excluded.

repo.description: Repository name — one of your connected repos.

entity.description: Function name, file path, or module name

depth.description: How many hops to trace (default: 3, range: 1–5)

tools.name: search_functions
tools.title: Search Functions
tools.description:
Find functions by name or concept across the whole codebase.

CALL THIS WHEN:
• Checking whether a function, helper or utility already exists
• Finding where something is implemented (e.g. "retry", "validate", "notify")

RETURNS: Matching functions with file path, line range, module, signature, export status and complexity. Matches name parts (camelCase, snake_case) and file paths, not comments; test code ranks last. SCREAMING_SNAKE queries, and queries no function matches, return matching constants with up to 80 characters of each value.

repo.description: Repository name — one of your connected repos.

query.description: Function name or part of one

file.description: Only this file (full path matches exactly, a file name as a substring)

tools.name: get_unused_code
tools.title: Unused Code
tools.description:
Find code nothing runs: functions no production entry point (endpoint, CLI command, cron job, event handler, worker, entry file) reaches.

CALL THIS WHEN:
• Cleaning up a module or deleting a function
• Confirming new code is reached from an entry point

RETURNS: Reachability through the call graph, not text references.
• Dead: unreached, named in no other file, and no production file imports its file.
• Possibly unused: unreached, but named in other files (string dispatch, dynamic loading) or its file is imported. Listed with the files that name it.
• Used only by tests: exported functions and class methods only test files reference.
With `functions`: each one's status, and the call path from an entry point when it's reachable.

repo.description: Repository name — one of your connected repos.

functions.description: Function names or Class.method names to check instead of listing everything unused

tools.name: pharaoh_account
tools.title: Account Status
tools.description:
Your Pharaoh plan and live repo in each workspace. Changes nothing.

CALL THIS WHEN:
• Checking which plan a workspace is on, or which repo is live
• A repo doesn't answer because it isn't live
• Upgrading so every repo is live, or managing billing

RETURNS: Each workspace you can access with its plan, live repo and tracked-repo count, the upgrade link for free workspaces, the setup page, and the billing page when a workspace has a billing account.

action.description: Only status; pharaoh_manage_repo switches the live repo or refreshes one

tools.name: pharaoh_manage_repo
tools.title: Switch or Refresh Live Repo
tools.description:
Switch a free workspace's live repo, or re-map a live repo now.

• set_free_repo { repo }: make repo the workspace's live repo. The previous live repo stops answering and refreshing; its graph is deleted after 30 days unless it is made live again.
• refresh_repo { repo, full? }: queue a re-map of one live repo. Live repos also re-map on every push.

CALL THIS WHEN:
• A repo doesn't answer because it isn't live, and the user wants it to be the live one
• A live repo's graph looks out of date, or needs a full rebuild

RETURNS: The new live repo and the repos no longer live, or the queued job.

full.description: refresh_repo only: rebuild the whole graph instead of a delta refresh
